open_points.subject: ClientViewer creation and access-link issuance authority
open_points.text: “created by an operator” and “issued and re-issuable by an operator” contradict R0-14: “Creating, revoking and re-issuing client viewers, their access links and project grants … all require the access-management capability, which only administrators hold.”
open_points.question: Can an operator create a ClientViewer or issue/reissue its access link, or are both actions administrator-only?
options: Operators may perform both actions
Only administrators may perform both actions
Creation and credential issuance have different authorities
open_points.default_guess: Only administrators may perform both actions.

witness.initial: An operator is assigned to project P but has no access-management capability.
events: The operator requests creation of a viewer and issuance of its first access link for P.
outcomes: The requests succeed because the Principals section assigns them to an operator.
The requests are denied because R0-14 reserves them to administrators.
witness.observer: The operator and the intended viewer

open_points.subject: Archived-project access revocation
open_points.text: “revoking one project grant closes only that project” and “Registry archival is independent from viewer-grant revocation” conflict with “An archived project is readable and immutable in the portal,” while R0-16 makes grants project-scoped records.
open_points.question: May administrators revoke or alter grants and assignments for an archived project despite the general archived-project immutability rule?
options: Security and access records remain mutable after archival
All project-scoped records, including grants and assignments, are immutable after archival
Revocation is allowed but other grant and assignment changes are forbidden
open_points.default_guess: Permit revocation after archival while forbidding new grants and ordinary business mutations.

witness.initial: Project P is archived while viewer V still has an active grant.
events: An administrator revokes V's grant to P.
outcomes: The revocation succeeds and V immediately loses access.
The revocation is rejected because P is archived and immutable, so V retains access.

open_points.subject: ClientViewer identifying data
open_points.text: “A permanent read-only viewer identity representing one client” does not name any client identifier, display label, or other input by which an administrator distinguishes that viewer.
open_points.question: What identifying facts must or may be supplied when a ClientViewer is created, and what uniqueness rules apply?
options: Only an opaque viewer ID
A required human-readable client name or label
A Registry or other external client identifier
A combination of opaque ID and administrator-maintained label
open_points.default_guess: Store an opaque viewer ID plus a required administrator-maintained display label.

witness.initial: Two unrelated clients each need access to project P and neither has a login email.
events: An administrator creates both ClientViewer records.
Later the administrator must select one viewer to revoke or grant another project.
outcomes: The API exposes sufficient identifying data to distinguish the viewers.
The records contain only opaque IDs, so the administrator must distinguish them using information not defined by the product text.

open_points.subject: Viewer access-link delivery
open_points.text: The credential is “issued and re-issuable” and administrators “manage … access links,” but no text says what observable output contains a newly issued link or how it reaches the client.
open_points.question: What does issuance return, to whom is the capability link revealed, how many times may it be retrieved, and is delivery to the client inside or outside the portal?
options: Return the full link once to the administrator for out-of-band delivery
Have the portal deliver the link through a named external system
Allow later retrieval of the current link
Return only a success result and require an unspecified external mechanism
open_points.default_guess: Return the full link exactly once to the administrator for out-of-band delivery.

witness.initial: Administrator A creates viewer V, who has no credential yet.
events: A issues V's first access credential.
The issuance response is returned successfully.
outcomes: The response reveals a one-time capability link that A can deliver to V.
The response contains only metadata, leaving no defined way for V to receive the secret.

open_points.subject: Staff email normalization
open_points.text: “mandatory unique normalized email as login identifier” does not define normalization or when uniqueness is checked.
open_points.question: Which transformations define the normalized email, and are create, ordinary email change, and recovery override all rejected on the same normalized collision rule?
options: Trim and case-fold the entire address
Trim and lowercase only the domain
Apply provider-specific canonicalization
Use another explicitly defined normalization
open_points.default_guess: Trim surrounding whitespace and Unicode-case-fold the entire address, applying the same uniqueness check to every email-changing action.

witness.initial: An active account exists for User@Example.com.
events: An administrator attempts to create another account for user@example.com.
outcomes: Creation is rejected because both normalize to the same login.
Creation succeeds because only the domain, or no part, is case-normalized.
witness.observer: The administrator and both account holders

open_points.subject: Service credential rotation overlap
open_points.text: Credentials are “rotatable with an overlap period,” but the period's source, start, end, and effect on existing credentials are not specified.
open_points.question: When rotation occurs, how long does the prior credential remain valid, can the administrator choose the duration, and may it be revoked before the overlap expires?
options: A fixed configured overlap begins at rotation
An administrator supplies an expiry for the old credential
Both credentials remain valid until explicit revocation
Rotation immediately revokes the old credential
open_points.default_guess: Use a deployment-configured overlap beginning at rotation, with explicit early revocation allowed.

witness.initial: Service principal S authenticates with credential C1.
events: An administrator rotates C1 and receives C2.
S continues using C1 during deployment of C2.
outcomes: C1 remains accepted for a defined overlap interval.
C1 is immediately rejected or remains valid indefinitely because no interval was defined.

open_points.subject: Service-principal source scope
open_points.text: A producer scope includes “allowed source types,” but no source-type vocabulary, location in the snapshot, or authorization comparison is named.
open_points.question: What is a source type, where does an import declare it, what values exist, and how is it matched against the principal's scope?
options: A closed enum carried in each snapshot
A value derived from source provenance
The concrete producer identity itself
Remove source type and scope only by project or administrative area
open_points.default_guess: Define a closed source-type enum carried explicitly in the snapshot and matched exactly against the principal's grants.

witness.initial: Principal S is allowed source type A for project P.
events: S imports a snapshot for P whose provenance can be interpreted as type B but has no explicit source-type field.
outcomes: The import is accepted because project scope alone is sufficient or type is inferred as A.
The import is rejected because the inferred provenance is type B.

open_points.subject: Closed role capability sets
open_points.text: “Roles map to closed capability sets” names only broad categories such as mutation and access management, without enumerating the capabilities or their mapping to each promised action.
open_points.question: What exact capabilities exist, which role holds each one, and which capability every staff action requires?
options: One project-mutation capability plus one access-management capability
Separate capabilities for each resource or action family
A fully enumerated capability matrix defined in this State 0 text
open_points.default_guess: Use separately named capabilities for each action family and publish an explicit role-to-capability matrix.

witness.initial: Administrator A is assigned no operator projects but holds the administrator role.
events: A attempts to correct an expense on project P.
outcomes: The action succeeds because administrators inherit all operator mutation capabilities.
The action is denied because administrator access management does not imply project mutation or assignment.

open_points.subject: Staff initial-password change
open_points.text: R0-19 says “the holder logs in with the initial password and changes it” but does not say whether the account is forced to change it before any other operation, or whether this is merely expected behavior.
open_points.question: Must an activated staff account change its administrator-supplied initial password before it can perform other authenticated actions?
options: Force password change before all other authenticated operations
Allow ordinary use immediately and leave the change voluntary
Force change only after a configured age
open_points.default_guess: Force a password change before any other authenticated operation.

witness.initial: A pending operator account is activated with its administrator-chosen initial password.
events: The holder logs in successfully.
Without changing the password, the holder attempts to create an expense.
outcomes: The expense is refused until the password is changed.
The expense succeeds because no mandatory-change state is specified.

open_points.subject: Confirmed OCR expense input
open_points.text: “confirmed normalized recognition result … supported contract_version, complete confirmed content” does not name the required content fields, their types, or what proves that content is confirmed.
open_points.question: What exact fields constitute the normalized recognition input, which are required, and how is confirmation represented and validated?
options: A closed versioned schema with an explicit confirmation field or status
Any provider-neutral JSON accepted as complete by the operator
A reference to data fetched from OCR
A schema deferred to a named later-state question
open_points.default_guess: Define a closed versioned schema with an explicit confirmed status and required monetary, document, and provenance fields.

witness.initial: An operator has an OCR result with document identity, total, date, and supplier but no explicit confirmation flag.
events: The operator submits it as an expense intake request.
outcomes: The portal accepts it because authenticated submission itself means confirmed.
The portal rejects it because an explicit confirmation fact is required.

open_points.subject: Recognized-document replay conflict
open_points.text: “One recognized document creates at most one Expense with one Document; replay is idempotent” does not define the result when the same recognized_document_id is replayed with different content, project, or allocation.
open_points.question: How must the portal respond when a recognized_document_id already exists but the replay differs from the accepted request?
options: Reject every differing replay as an integrity conflict
Return the original result and ignore differences
Permit allocation changes while rejecting document or project changes
Treat the submission as an expense correction
open_points.default_guess: Reject any differing replay as an integrity conflict and return the existing result only for an identical replay.

witness.initial: recognized_document_id D created expense E in project P for EUR 100.
events: A staff member submits D again for project P with a total of EUR 120 and a different allocation.
outcomes: The request returns E idempotently and silently ignores the differences.
The request is rejected as an integrity conflict.
witness.observer: The submitting staff member and client viewing totals

open_points.subject: Payment identity collision
open_points.text: “register work payments (idempotent by stable payment identity)” does not define whether idempotency requires identical content or what happens when the identity is reused with another amount, date, or project.
open_points.question: What comparison and failure apply when a stable payment identity is submitted more than once with different content?
options: Reject differing content as an integrity conflict
Return the original payment and ignore differences
Update the existing payment
Define mutable and immutable payment fields separately
open_points.default_guess: Return the original payment for an identical replay and reject differing content as an integrity conflict.

witness.initial: Payment identity PAY-1 exists in project P for EUR 1,000.
events: An operator submits PAY-1 again for EUR 1,500.
outcomes: The existing EUR 1,000 payment is returned without error.
The request is rejected because PAY-1 is bound to different content.
witness.observer: The operator and client viewing the work balance

open_points.subject: Expense correction action
open_points.text: “an operator can: correct … an expense” does not say which stored facts are correctable, whether document provenance and recognized identity are immutable, or what validations and result the correction has.
open_points.question: Which expense fields may be corrected, which are immutable, and does correcting the total require an atomic replacement of allocations?
options: Allow correction of all normalized business fields except identity and provenance
Allow only a closed subset such as date, supplier, description, and total
Create a replacement expense instead of mutating the existing one
Define correction as a later-state command with an explicit field matrix
open_points.default_guess: Keep identity and provenance immutable; allow a closed set of business-field corrections and require allocations to balance atomically when the total changes.

witness.initial: Expense E totals EUR 100 and has allocations totaling EUR 100.
events: An operator corrects E's total to EUR 120 without supplying new allocations.
outcomes: The correction succeeds and leaves temporarily or permanently unbalanced allocations.
The correction is rejected unless replacement allocations totaling EUR 120 are supplied atomically.
witness.observer: The operator and client viewing totals

open_points.subject: Unavailable-data representation
open_points.text: “Unavailable data is shown explicitly, never fabricated or replaced by silent zeros” does not define the JSON representation or distinguish absent, not-applicable, temporarily unavailable, and forbidden data.
open_points.question: How does each API response represent unavailable values and their reason?
options: Null plus a machine-readable reason code
Omit the field and include an errors or availability collection
Return a typed unavailable object in place of the value
Use endpoint-level error responses for temporary unavailability
open_points.default_guess: Return null with a closed machine-readable availability reason for every unavailable value.

witness.initial: Project P has no planned work cost, so overall progress is unavailable.
events: Viewer V requests P's project summary.
outcomes: overall_progress is null with an explicit reason such as no_planned_work.
The field is omitted or represented by a different sentinel while still being considered explicit by the implementer.
witness.observer: The frontend consuming the JSON API

open_points.subject: Progress precision and derived-value rounding order
open_points.text: “manual work progress per section (0–100%)” and “rounded half up to two places” do not define allowed percentage precision or whether section values are rounded before or after aggregation.
open_points.question: What precision is accepted for completion percentages, and at which steps are completed-work value, weighted progress, and totals rounded?
options: Accept decimal percentages and round each section's money before summing
Accept decimal percentages and round only final displayed totals
Accept whole-number percentages only
Define separate storage and presentation precision rules
open_points.default_guess: Accept percentages to a defined decimal scale, compute at full decimal precision, and round final monetary outputs half up to two places.

witness.initial: Two sections have planned work amounts whose percentage products contain fractions of a cent.
events: An operator records fractional completion percentages.
A viewer requests completed work value and overall progress.
outcomes: Each section is rounded first and the rounded values are summed.
Unrounded section values are summed and only the final total is rounded, producing a different cent value.

open_points.subject: Audit coverage and transaction failure
open_points.text: “Every significant action records actor provenance” does not define significant action exhaustively or state whether a business action must fail and roll back when its audit record cannot be written.
open_points.question: Which successful and failed actions must be audited, and is audit persistence atomic with every state-changing business action?
options: Audit every mutation and security attempt atomically; failure rolls back the action
Audit only the listed successful actions atomically
Allow the business action to succeed if audit persistence fails
Use a durable asynchronous audit mechanism with defined recovery
open_points.default_guess: Audit every mutation and material security attempt atomically, rolling back a mutation if its audit record cannot be stored.

witness.initial: Expense E exists and the audit store cannot accept another record.
events: An operator changes E from included to excluded.
outcomes: The expense change is rolled back and the request fails because the audit record is mandatory.
The expense change succeeds while the audit record is missing or deferred.
witness.observer: The operator, client, and later auditor

open_points.subject: Registry HTTP contract and failure translation
open_points.text: The portal consumes “the confirmed HTTP boundary … per the platform Registry contract” with “typed failure translation,” but the request and response schemas, lifecycle responses, timeout behavior, and translated failure types are not present in the text.
open_points.question: What exact Registry inputs, outputs, and failure mappings must later states and code implement for active-project listing, validation, and context lookup?
options: Reproduce the complete Registry contract in these accepted texts
Name a versioned immutable external contract artifact that later agents receive
Define the required subset and all translated failures here
open_points.default_guess: Define the required subset and a closed mapping for not found, archived, unauthorized, unavailable, timeout, and malformed responses in these texts.

witness.initial: An authenticated administrator lists active Registry projects while Registry is unavailable.
events: The portal's Registry request times out.
outcomes: The portal returns a typed dependency-unavailable error.
The portal returns an empty list, a generic internal error, or another locally chosen translation.

open_points.subject: Mandatory but deferred Email Delivery Gateway
open_points.text: R0-03 calls the Email Delivery Gateway “a mandatory external boundary,” while the External systems section says it “is called by no operation of the running portal.”
open_points.question: Must a current deployment configure and validate an Email Delivery Gateway even though every mail-producing operation is inert?
options: Startup requires valid gateway configuration now
Gateway configuration is optional until Q19 is implemented
A no-op gateway must be configured
The gateway is architecturally mandatory but explicitly excluded from current startup validation
open_points.default_guess: Do not require gateway configuration until an operation can call it, while retaining it as the mandatory future delivery boundary.

witness.initial: A deployment provides all database, binary-root, host, and origin settings but no email-gateway settings.
events: The service starts while R0-23 remains in force.
outcomes: Startup succeeds because no running operation can use the gateway.
Startup fails configuration validation because R0-03 makes the gateway mandatory.
witness.observer: The host operator and deployment health monitor

open_points.subject: Password-reset and challenge authority
open_points.text: R0-06 promises that “a staff member may request a password reset,” and R0-15 says challenge endpoints “prove their own authority … [with] a single-use token,” while R0-23 says issuing or completing these challenges “answer with the concealed authentication rejection and read, write, audit and deliver nothing” and a reset request “does nothing.”
open_points.question: For the accepted current product, are password reset and the other challenge endpoints functional authority-bearing actions or deliberately inert rejected operations?
options: All challenge operations are inert until Q19 is implemented
Password reset is functional but verification and email-change challenges are inert
All operations follow R0-06 and R0-15 now
Separate current behavior from the future designed policy explicitly
open_points.default_guess: Treat all challenge operations as inert current behavior and label R0-06 and the authority sentence in R0-15 as future policy.

witness.initial: Active staff member S has forgotten the password and controls the account email address.
events: S requests a password reset.
S attempts to complete it using whatever token the functional reading would issue.
outcomes: A token is created and delivered, and S can set a new password under R0-06 and R0-15.
The request reveals nothing and creates or sends nothing; completion returns concealed rejection under R0-23.
witness.observer: Staff member S and the Email Delivery Gateway

open_points.subject: Health-check semantics
open_points.text: R0-11 says the service “answers an unauthenticated liveness and readiness check” but does not define their success bodies/statuses, what readiness tests, or their failure statuses.
open_points.question: What conditions make liveness and readiness succeed or fail, and what exact non-sensitive HTTP responses represent each result?
options: Liveness tests only the process; readiness tests database, binary root, and required configuration
Both checks report only that the HTTP process is running
Readiness tests only database access
Define another closed dependency set and response contract
open_points.default_guess: Liveness reports process availability; readiness verifies database access, binary-root readability, and validated configuration, returning fixed minimal bodies and 200/503 statuses.

witness.initial: The HTTP process is running but the SQLite database cannot be opened.
events: An orchestrator calls both health endpoints.
outcomes: Liveness returns success and readiness returns failure.
Both return success because dependency checks were not defined.

open_points.subject: Concealed binary-read response
open_points.text: R0-12 says unknown, cross-project, hidden, oversize, and unlisted reads are “answered the same way” but does not state the shared HTTP status, headers, or body.
open_points.question: What exact indistinguishable response is returned for every concealed binary-read failure, and how are storage I/O failures handled?
options: A fixed 404 response with no distinguishing body or headers
A fixed 403 response
A fixed generic authentication rejection
One concealed response for authorization/object cases and a separate dependency error for storage failure
open_points.default_guess: Return a fixed 404 response for all concealed object, authorization, visibility, size, and media-type cases, with a separate non-disclosing server error for unexpected storage failure.

witness.initial: Viewer V may access project P but photo H in P is hidden.
events: V requests H's binary download.
outcomes: The portal returns a fixed 404 response.
The portal returns a fixed 403 or another response chosen by the implementer; both satisfy only the stated indistinguishability requirement.

open_points.subject: Bootstrap command exit-code contract
open_points.text: R0-07 requires “a closed set of exit codes that deployment scripts may branch on” but does not name the codes or map them to success and failures; it also excludes arguments, environment, and files without naming the input channel.
open_points.question: How does the command securely obtain email and password, and what exact exit code corresponds to success, existing staff, invalid input, configuration failure, and persistence failure?
options: Interactive terminal prompts with a documented exit-code table
Standard input with a documented exit-code table
Operating-system credential channel or secret broker
Another explicitly named non-argument input mechanism
open_points.default_guess: Read both values from non-echoing interactive prompts and define a stable exit-code table for every outcome.

witness.initial: The database already contains one staff account.
events: A deployment script runs the bootstrap command and supplies valid new administrator credentials.
outcomes: The command exits with a dedicated already-initialized code that the script handles safely.
The command exits with a generic failure code indistinguishable from malformed input or database failure.
witness.observer: The deployment script and host operator
